proposals.before: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's grandson Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
proposals.after: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's son Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 寅子樞 means Yin's son Shu, not grandson; the literal already has son.

proposals.before: His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
proposals.after: His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
proposals.reason: 追贈 is a posthumous official grant, not an enfeoffment of land or fief.

proposals.before: For more than twenty years the realm has endured deep trial; through that anguish Heaven has prepared a sage ruler—and today is the day.
proposals.after: For more than twenty years he has upheld primal rectitude over the myriad states; through grave anguish Heaven opens the way to sage rule—and today is that day.
proposals.reason: 元貞萬國 refers to the heir's long upright stewardship of the realm, not merely that the realm endured trial; the idiomatic rendering drops that sense.

proposals.before: The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor, and granted five hundred bolts of funeral silk and five hundred shi of grain.
proposals.after: The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant, and granted five hundred bolts of funeral silk and five hundred shi of grain.
proposals.reason: 贈太尉 is the posthumous honor Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: The sovereign mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor, and granted funeral silks of five hundred bolts and five hundred shi of grain.
proposals.after: The sovereign mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant, and granted funeral silks of five hundred bolts and five hundred shi of grain.
proposals.reason: 贈太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Mentor; also 贈 is posthumous honor more than enfeoffment.

proposals.before: When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting secretary, right assistant in the Secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.
proposals.after: When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed supervising secretary, right assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and vice minister of personnel.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Drafting Secretary (中書舍人); 尚書右丞 is Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: When Suzong ascended the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed Drafting Secretary, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: When Suzong ascended the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary, Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary; 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Zunqing's son Xiang—Pei Xiang, styled Suren—through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to secretary for discussion of the heir apparent.
proposals.after: Zunqing's son Xiang (Pei Xiang), styled Suren, through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to secretary for discussion of the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遵慶子向子向 is a corrupted biography formula for 遵慶子向; the em-dash duplicate 'Xiang—Pei Xiang' should be a single identification.

proposals.before: Zunqing's son Xiang—Pei Xiang, styled Suren—through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to Secretary for Discussion of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: Zunqing's son Xiang (Pei Xiang), styled Suren, through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to Secretary for Discussion of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: Same corruption of 向子向 produces an unnatural duplicated English name in the literal field.

proposals.before: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
proposals.after: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
proposals.reason: 李懷光 is standardly Li Huaiguang; the apostrophe in Huai'guang is unnatural English romanization.

proposals.before: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
proposals.after: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
proposals.reason: Same unnatural Huai'guang romanization in the literal field.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as junior mentor to the heir apparent.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title of junior mentor to the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 贈 is a posthumous title grant, not a territorial enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 贈 as enfeoffment in the literal field.

proposals.before: In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate of the heir apparent, soon sent out as prefect of She.
proposals.after: In Dashun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate of the heir apparent, soon sent out as prefect of She.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun.

proposals.before: In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
proposals.after: In Dashun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
proposals.reason: Same reign-name error Dazhun for 大順/Dashun in the literal field.

proposals.before: Zunqing and his son and grandson—few could match them.
proposals.after: Zunqing and his son—few could match them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 父子 denotes father and son(s); the literal invents a grandson not present in the source.

proposals.before: Zunqing and his line—few could equal them.
proposals.after: Zunqing and his son—few could equal them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 父子 is specifically the father-son pair, not a vague family line.

proposals.before: He therefore held it and would not issue it.
proposals.after: He therefore withheld it and would not issue it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 持之不下 means withholding the appointment; literal 'held it' obscures the refusal to issue.

decisions.reason: s0001 寅子樞 is Yin's son Shu; grandson invents a generation beyond 子.
s0003 追贈禮部尚書 is a posthumous office grant; 追贈 is not territorial enfeoffment (封), and the replacement states that accurately.
s0106 元貞萬國，二十余年 names long upright stewardship of the myriad states; the original drops that sense and folds the twenty years into 殷憂 alone. The replacement restores both halves before 殷憂啟聖.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖

decisions.reason: s0134 贈太尉 is the posthumous honor Grand Commandant; Grand Mentor would be 太傅, so the title must be corrected.
Same unit: 贈太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Mentor, and 贈 marks posthumous honor rather than enfeoffment.
s0144 給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Drafting Secretary (中書舍人); 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Secretariat.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 給事中、尚書右丞、吏部侍郎

decisions.reason: Same unit: 給事中 and 尚書右丞 are Supervising Secretary and Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs; the literal replacement matches those offices.
s0158 identifies 遵慶子向, 字傃仁; "Zunqing's son Xiang—Pei Xiang, styled Suren" already names him correctly. Changing the em-dash to parentheses is stylistic and does not remove any semantic error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遵慶子 向子向，字傃仁

decisions.reason: The same lemma formula already yields a correct identification of Xiang (Pei Xiang), styled Suren; the literal punctuation tweak is stylistic only.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遵慶子 向子向，字傃仁

decisions.reason: 李懷光 is Li Huaiguang; the apostrophe in Huai'guang is nonstandard pinyin (not needed before g) and should be removed.
Same unit: 李懷光 is Li Huaiguang; the literal field should drop the misplaced apostrophe.
s0178 贈太子少保 is a posthumous title grant; 贈 is not territorial enfeoffment.
Same unit: 贈 marks a posthumous title grant, not enfeoffment; the literal replacement matches that sense.
s0188 大順 is the Tang reign Dashun; Dazhun misreads 順.
Same unit: 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun; the literal replacement restores the reign name.
s0223 遵慶父子 is Zunqing and his son(s); "son and grandson" invents a generation absent from 父子.
父子 names the father-son pair, not a vague multi-generation "line"; "Zunqing and his son" matches the Chinese.
持之不下 is already covered by "held it and would not issue it"; "withheld" only restyles the same refusal already stated in "would not issue it."

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0010/r0011 show English Li Huai'guang came only from the misplaced apostrophe; the personal-name claim must use Li Huaiguang while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
